defects: Conclusion is asserting global boundedness of f on the entire upper half-plane (∃ B, ∀ τ with Im τ > 0, ‖f τ‖ ≤ B) instead of the gold's IsBoundedAtImInfty f, which only requires f to be bounded near the cusp i∞ (as Im τ → ∞), matching a filter-based/eventual notion of boundedness. This is a strictly stronger and generally false claim — e.g. c_m = 1 for all m gives f(τ) = 1/(1-q), which converges (is Summable) for every τ in the upper half-plane but is unbounded as Im τ → 0+, so the produced statement's conclusion does not follow from the hypotheses in general.

This mismatch also misrepresents the informal statement itself, which specifically asks for boundedness 'at the cusp i∞' (a local/asymptotic condition), not global boundedness on the whole upper half-plane.

f's domain is given as unbundled ℂ → ℂ with an explicit positivity-of-imaginary-part side condition rather than the bundled ℍ → ℂ type used in gold; this alone is a benign reformulation but is listed since it interacts with the conclusion's domain of quantification.
